description: COSMOGUARD aims to develop intelligent health-monitoring software to track astronauts’ vital signs, detect potential health risks, and provide timely alerts during space missions. Our mission is to make space exploration safer through innovative technology and real-time health monitoring.
summary:
ASTROHEALTH – An Intelligent Wearable-Based Health Monitoring and Decision Support System for Astronauts

ASTROHEALTH is an AI-powered health monitoring system designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It integrates wearable sensors with intelligent software to collect and analyse vital health indicators such as heart rate, ECG, blood oxygen levels, body temperature, sleep patterns and physical activity. The system monitors changes in astronauts' health, identifies potential risks associated with microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation and the space environment, and provides personalised health recommendations and real-time alerts. It also maintains individual health records and provides a dashboard for monitoring health trends. The primary objective is to empower astronauts to independently assess, manage and respond to their health conditions, improving crew safety and well-being during space missions.
details: ASTROHEALTH is an intelligent wearable-based health monitoring and decision support system designed to monitor and improve the health, safety and well-being of astronauts during long-duration space missions. Astronauts face several health challenges due to microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation, confinement and changes in their daily routines. To address these challenges, ASTROHEALTH combines wearable sensors with an AI-powered software platform to collect and analyse important health parameters such as heart rate, ECG, blood oxygen level (SpO₂), skin temperature, physical activity and sleep patterns. Environmental sensors can also monitor cabin conditions such as temperature, humidity and carbon dioxide levels, while a dedicated radiation dosimeter can measure radiation exposure. The collected data is transmitted to the software platform, where it is analysed and compared with each astronaut's personal health baseline to identify unusual patterns and potential health risks. The system provides real-time alerts, personalised recommendations and a digital dashboard displaying health status, trends and medical history, helping astronauts monitor their condition and take appropriate action. The major benefits include continuous health monitoring, early identification of potential health problems, personalised health analysis, improved self-management, long-term health records and better health-related decision-making during missions. The intended impact is to reduce health risks, support astronaut independence and contribute to safer and more sustainable space exploration, including future lunar and Mars missions. The proposed development technologies include an ESP32 microcontroller, MAX30102 sensor for heart rate and SpO₂ monitoring, AD8232 ECG sensor, temperature sensors, environmental sensors and a radiation dosimeter. Python is proposed for data analysis and AI development, C/C++ for embedded programming, Scikit-learn or TensorFlow for machine learning, Streamlit for the health dashboard and SQLite or PostgreSQL for storing health records. Bluetooth or Wi-Fi may be used for communication in the prototype. The creativity and innovation of ASTROHEALTH lie in its integration of wearable health monitoring, artificial intelligence and personalised health analysis into a single platform. Unlike basic health monitoring systems that only display measurements, ASTROHEALTH compares readings with individual health baselines, identifies unusual changes and provides useful alerts and suggested actions. During development, the team considered factors such as sensor accuracy, system reliability, astronaut safety, space environmental conditions, power efficiency, wearable comfort, data security, real-time performance, individual health differences, scalability and cost. The system also recognises the limitations of wearable technology, as conditions such as bone-density loss and immune-system changes require specialised tests or validated indirect indicators rather than ordinary smartwatch sensors. The project is currently a prototype concept demonstrated using simulated health readings, and further development, testing and validation would be required before actual spaceflight use. Overall, ASTROHEALTH aims to make astronaut health monitoring smarter, more personalised and more reliable, helping astronauts maintain their health and safety throughout long-duration space missions.
